podcast.body: A multi-part song from the 1977 album *Farewell to Kings*. This track showcases Rush's musical prowess and Neil Peart's lyrical capabilities. The story within the song, detailing an astronaut's journey to investigate a black hole, was conceived by Peart after he read an article on black holes in *Time* magazine. The narrative continues with "Cygnus X-1 Book II" on the *Hemispheres* album. "Signus X1 from the Farewell the Kings album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This Rush song is identified as one that features the "devil's tri tone" (flattened fifth), demonstrating the Canadian progressive rock band's use of this distinctive interval in their compositions. "In addition to a ton of Sabbath and Hendrix songs, they can also be heard in David Bowie's station to station, the beautiful people by Marilyn Manson, Blurred Girls and Boys, SIGDIS X1 and YYZ by Rush, Enter Sandman from Metallica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
